tagline: Past one enormous aspen to a lake in a sunken valley.
intro: The byway leaves Highway 24 north of Loa and climbs, entering the Fishlake National Forest within four miles, then drops a little to the lake. Past the resorts it runs through meadow and sagebrush flats at the unspoiled north end, by Johnson Valley Reservoir, and comes down a long, drier slope of pinyon and juniper to Highway 72.
The geologist Clarence Dutton saw the lake in 1875 and wrote that no resort more beautiful could be found in southern Utah, with Mounts Marvine and Hilgard standing in the distance.
season: Fall, when the dense stands of aspen make the drive especially attractive.

moments.title: Pando
moments.text: A mile southwest of the lake the highway passes Pando, some 47,000 aspen stems on a single root system, generally held to be the largest organism on Earth by weight.

moments.title: Fish Lake
moments.text: Utah's largest natural mountain lake fills a graben, a down-faulted valley, under the Mytoge Mountains, which rise sharply about a thousand feet off its southeast shore.

moments.title: Johnson Valley Reservoir
moments.text: The road drops to a square mile of water where the Fremont River begins, and crosses that young river a little farther on at Zedds Meadow.

practical: The roads are paved and suitable for all vehicles, but heavy snow can be a problem in winter between Fish Lake and Highway 72.

sources.label: Visit Utah, A Forest Oasis in the Heart of the Desert
